text:
riley: Hey team, just got a surprise bill from the ER visit last week. Hospital was in-network but the ER doctor is listed as out-of-network and billed me a $420 balance. EOB says facility covered but professional provider denied as OON. Has anyone dealt with this?
maya (People Ops): Ugh, that sounds like a surprise billing / balance bill case. First, check the EOB for the claim type: facility vs professional. If facility was in-network and the clinician was truly out-of-network, federal/state surprise billing rules may protect you. You should file a billing dispute with the insurer and the provider.
riley: What docs do they want? I have the itemized bill and EOB. No idea how to prove the hospital was in-network.
maya (People Ops): Minimal packet: 1) EOB showing insurer paid facility portion 2) Itemized hospital bill showing clinician charge 3) Proof of in-network hospital (screenshot from Anthem provider search or hospital bill header) 4) Short cover note requesting dispute under surprise billing protections. Use the insurer dispute portal or call member services and ask for "balance bill dispute".
billing-bot: Reminder: Upload claims docs at Benefits Portal -> Claims -> Disputes within 60 days of EOB to preserve appeal rights. Include PDF of itemized bill + EOB.
anthem-support: Hi Riley 37 we can escalate this. Please DM member ID, claim numbers for facility and professional lines, and attach the itemized bill + EOB. We'll initiate a manual review for possible "continuity of care/surprise billing" protections. Typical review window 7-30 business days.
provider-billing: Hi @riley, I'm from the ER group billing team. Sometimes the clinician bills separately because they're contracted differently. If you'd like, DM the bill number and I can check whether the clinician has an in-network contract or if the charge can be adjusted. If it's an emergency, many payers cover at in-network rates per regulations.
riley: Thanks! Quick q: will this hit my deductible while disputed? I already hit part of my deductible this year and worried about extra OOP.
maya (People Ops): Good question. If insurer reprocesses the professional claim as in-network, your OOP should be reconciled and any member responsibility refunded/credited. During dispute it may show as pending; if you paid already, you can request reimbursement. We can help with wording for the dispute note.
riley: Could I forward the hospital intake form that shows hospital location/physician group as proof?
maya (People Ops): Yes, include intake forms and any admission/visit summary that ties the clinician to the event at the in-network facility. Also include a short note: "Patient was seen in an in-network facility for emergency care; provider billed separately as out-of-network. Requesting balance bill review under surprise billing protections."
anthem-support: Also note: if the claim involves emergency services, plan must apply in-network cost-sharing even if provider is OON, per federal rules. We'll need the claim details to proceed.
riley: Okay I'll gather EOB, itemized bill, intake form, and hospital provider search screenshot and DM them. Appreciate the help.
provider-billing: If you want me to try a courtesy adjustment, DM the bill # and we can review internal coding before insurer reprocess.
maya (People Ops): If you run into any trouble getting documents, ping me and I can coordinate with Anthem on your behalf. :thumbsup:
